content.title: Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick Says She Returned to Survivor 50 to Honor Her Late Brothers (Exclusive)
content.text: Key PointsStephenie returns to Survivor aiming for a quieter, more strategic and honorable gameplay.Family, past losses, and honoring her brothers motivate her participation in Survivor 50.She plans alliances carefully, hoping her reputation and experience benefit her game. To say a lot has happened to Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick in the last 16 years would be an understatement. Gone are the days of filet mignon pizza, supplanted by family dinner nights. But, a few years ago, the 45-year-old was brought out of reality TV “retirement” to appear in Snake in the Grass and The Traitors — both alongside fellow Season 50 contestant Cirie Fields. That gave the former fan-favorite the confidence to come back to the island, eager to play as a quieter, more strategically-savvy version of the Stephenie we remember from decades ago. Her ultimate goal, however, is to have a game her kids are proud of, one to properly honor the memory of her two brothers she lost since last competing. Read on for my interview with Stephenie, and check in with Parade daily for interviews with this season’s contestants and other tidbits. Survivor 50 premieres on Feb. 25 with a three-hour episode on CBS. 🔥Don’t miss our weekly Survivor newsletter! Sign up to get Mike Bloom’s exclusive interviews with the players and the latest news about the show right to your inbox. 🔥 Survivor 50 interview with Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick The last time we saw you on Survivor, you were hocking filet mignon pizza on live TV. So what has life been like for you the past 15 years between trips to the island?Oh my gosh. Well, I was engaged then, so I got married after that. And shortly after that, had my first child, Sophia; she’s 13 now. And then I had a son; he’s 11. And then I had another daughter; she’s six. We sold the restaurant, so sadly, no more filet mignon pizza from Gigi’s. I had it for about five years, and it was just too hard to keep and move all over the country. My husband played baseball at the time, and we moved three times a year, so it was a lot. And that’s kind of why I “retired,” or whatever you want to call it, from reality TV, because his life became mine. And, as a professional athlete, it’s a really demanding life. The wife really holds down the fort. They’re always gone. And so with little kids at home and two dogs and moving three times a year. I mean, I had some offers come my way. But mommy and daddy both could not be gone, and so I hung up my hat for a little bit. And then, I guess about three years ago, reality TV came a-knockin’. And I did Snake in the Grass. I said no at first, but then I decided, “I’ll give it a shot. It’s only 10 days.” Kyle’s now retired and around, so it’s not like we’re both negligent parents and going off. [Like] he’s working, and I’m just doing reality TV, and we’re leaving our kids with some nanny or something. Daddy was home. So it was time to kind of get back in and see if I still had it. So I did Snake in the Grass. I lost. Cirie was there; she figured out I was the snake. She knows me too well for spending a month together in Fiji after Heroes vs. Villains. And then after that, I took a little more time off, went back to just being a mom. I worked at the kids’ school. I still work at their school. I do sales part-time; I do a couple of things. And then Traitors called. And I got the call. I was in the car with my son, and I have the guy on speaker, because I was driving. And I was like, “That sounds amazing. I have to say no. I can’t do it.” It was the day of myson’s first Holy Communion luncheon, the day I needed to fly out. And my whole family was coming; I was already committed. I hang up the phone. My son’s like, “Mom, that sounds so fun. You should do that. That’s so cool! A castle in Scotland game of Clue? You should do it!” So I go home, talk to my husband. He’s like, “Yeah, if you want to do it, do it.” I’m like, “Are you serious?!” Literally, two weeks later, I was on a plane to Scotland. As you’re talking about, you’ve gotten your feet wet on reality TV again over the past few years. What are you taking away from those experiences as you get back into Survivor?So Traitors and Snake in the Grass are totally different from Survivor And it was actually a really good refresher for me. In Traitors, I knew nobody except Cirie and Rachel from Snake in the Grass. But you literally can trust no one, much like Survivor. But in the game of Traitors, you kind of need to trust someone. So I decided to trust Cirie and Rachel, because those were the people I knew. And Cirie was a Traitor in the end, but she kept me just as safe as I kept her safe for nine out of 10 episodes. And right as I really started to figure it out, she got rid of me. And good gameplay to her. She did what she had to do. She’s still, to this day, the only Traitor that’s ever won, and that’s a hard job. The way she had to just lie to everybody, she did an unbelievable job. But it was really a good test for me, because I kind of had to play a little bit more of a quieter Stephenie and sit back and just observe and kind of feel people out. And not being on Survivor in almost 16 years now, I think that’s kind of the route I need to take. I’ll be myself for sure; I can’t be somebody that I’m not. But I’m also going to try to blend in a little. But because I was on it three times, I was a huge threat back in my 20s when I was on. I’m still pretty physically fit, and I don’t want people to feel threatened by that. I want to be the person that people enjoy being around and want to talk to. And I also contribute to camp, and I’m good in challenges. I’m not a threat to them. So it’s going to be kind of a fine line for me this time, but that’s kind of how I’ve got to play this game. Let’s talk about your reputation coming in here. Because it can’t be mentioned enough how much “Stephenie fever” was at its peak during your first two seasons. It was to the point where contestants in Guatemala were saying they applied for the show because of your journey on Palau. Do you feel that’s something that’s going to work for or against you this time around?I really hope it works for me. Because that’s who I was in my 20s. And I came out here just like everybody else, not knowing what to expect, and just giving it my all and never giving up and being a team player, just fighting for the team. And I’m still that person. I’m still a very loyal person. Did I have to stab some people in the back in Guatemala? Yes, I did, but that’s the game of Survivor. And in the new era, that’s applauded. So do I want to play that type of a game this time around? Absolutely not. I have three kids watching. I want to play a very honorable game, and I want to be truthful. But at the same time, I need to do what I need to do to get further in the game. And my children will understand that, and so will their school and friends. So I think my reputation is going to help me. I think there’s going to be people here that are going to want to work with me, and they’re going to like the Stephenie that played way back when. And they’re not going to think the 45-year-old Stephenie that played awesome then is a huge threat now to them. I think they’re going to want to want to keep me around at least enough until the going gets tough. And then we have to start making some moves, and then I’ll reassess it. I’m not going to sit here and worry myself sick over it, though. Because mentally, you can take yourself out of the game before the game even begins. Stephenie LaGrossa Kendrick on ‘Survivor 50’Robert Voets/CBS Related: Meet the Full Cast of Survivor 50Well, let’s talk about some of these people who will hopefully want to work with you. We’re gonna play a game called “Friend or Foe.” I’m going to give you a name of someone on the cast, and you have to tell me if they’re someone you want to work with, or someone you see as an enemy or threat. Starting with Jenna.I think Jenna can be a Friend. She’s an old-schooler. She hasn’t played since Season [8], so it’s been a long time, and she’s a mom. I think we’re gonna hit it off. How about your former Hero and ally, Colby?100% [Friend]. I mean, he stood up for me against the bully James way back when. And I haven’t seen or heard from him; I don’t think he’s really on social media. And we weren’t on social media then; it wasn’t even a thing. So I don’t have this huge social media presence either, but I think he’s gonna be a huge Friend.Alright, let’s open Pandora’s Box. How do you feel about Cirie?I think Cirie is gonna be a big Friend of mine out here. I think Cirie is going to have a way bigger target than I have on me. She won Traitors. She’s already played four times. She’s proven to be brutal in the game. Like brutal in a good way, like, a huge threat. If that girl goes far, she’s winning the whole thing; they’re not fools. And then she played Big Brother with her son and kept it a secret. She’s done way more TV than me. So she’s going to be a huge threat out here, and she’s going to be a great shield for me. So she’s going to be a very good friend of mine. A nice mea culpa for Scotland, maybe. How about Ozzy?I don’t really know Ozzy. But I always loved him, and I would really like to play with him. I always would love to play the game with Ozzy, and I hope he’s on my tribe. So I think Ozzy will be a Friend. Coach.Coach, definitely a Friend. I loved Coach. I had never met Coach. I still don’t understand why he was on the Villains tribe. Music to his ears!Seriously, I just think he’s a great guy. I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he’ll want to play an honorable game. He has kids now. I don’t know Coach from Adam, but Friend. Aubry.I want to get to know her. I don’t know her at all. But, if I’m correct, she played with Cirie. So if I have Cirie, I think I can have Aubry.Chrissy.Chrissy reminds me of just like a really cool mom. She, I know, had kids then older than my kids, so they must be older now. She’s super smart. So I think Chrissy would be a good Friend of mine. I think she got a raw deal. She played, and she went out far, just like me, and then she got screwed. Angelina.Angelina is hard for me to read. I want to get to know her. I want to like her. I know she’s a mom. I know she’s all for women’s and girls’ empowerment and things like that. But she hasn’t made much eye contact with me. I feel like she’s super in with the newbies. And I feel like I’m very old school and potentially could be a threat to her, and that worries me. So I will try to befriend her, and if she does not bite, she will become a Foe. Christian.Christian cracks me up. I want to be friends with him, and I want to be on his tribe. Because he’s fabulous, he’s so smart, and he would be great at puzzles. But I think he’s in with Angelina. And if Angelina is not going to want to work with me. I think I’m going to be on the outs there. Mike.Same with Mike White. He cracks me up. I love The White Lotus. I watch it, just like everybody else in the world. I just think he’s a funny guy. I think he’s a brilliant guy. I would love to get to know him. I hope, again, they’re gonna want to get to know me, and he will be my Friend. Otherwise, he’s a Foe. Rick.Rick Devens has been smiling at me from the second he got here, ear to ear. So I think Rick wants to work with me. Rick could be smiling at everybody ear to ear, I don’t know. I’m gonna follow him, because he’s really good at finding idols. [Laughs.] I’m just gonna be like, “Show me the way. Teach me! We didn’t have all this stuff back in my day.” So I’m hoping he’s a Friend. If not, he’s gotta go. Related: The 50 Best ‘Survivor’ Challenges Ever — According to the People Who Made Them (Exclusive) Alright, let’s get into these “newbies.” Starting with Jonathan.Love Jonathan, Friend. 100% need him on my tribe. Need him in my life. Love him. Love everything about him on the show. Provider, beast, good person, great to be around. Easy yes. Dee.I don’t know much about Dee. She looks like a brick s—thouse, though. Holy s—t! In my best day, I don’t look like that, and I was fit! But, again, good shield for me. She was a winner. She won the million, you’re gonna let her stay in the game and hand her another million potentially? I’ll keep her around. Emily.Emily, I like. She just seems so quiet and keeps to herself, smart. Again, I don’t need to be with all the jocks and the men and all that. I like to get to know people. So I would like to get to know somebody like Emily and Christian and Genevieve. Charlie.Charlie seems so quiet. I was thinking, coming out here, Charlie would want to work with somebody like me, but he hasn’t even looked at me. [Laughs.] Maybe people are just nervous. Old school, when we were at Ponderosa, nobody knew anybody. And that’s all you had, was to look at somebody in a first impression and a wink. And either he’s already got his crew, which I think he’s smarter than that. Because it doesn’t matter if you have your crew. Things are going to be like this [Snaps.] in a second. Nixxed, done, whatever. I don’t even know. Advantage in the tree, on the thing, on the tent, whatever. How about Q?Q worries me. Because I feel like Q is in with everybody, or tried to get in with everybody. Because I only say that because he reached out to me on Instagram. He friended me, and then he reached out to me, but then he never said anything about the game. He just commented like, “Hi, how are you?” So I either thumbs-upped it or just ignored it. So maybe he’s pissed, maybe because I didn’t bite, was like, “Hey, are you on 50?” I wasn’t gonna freaking say that, but he didn’t either. So now, since I’ve been here, the guy hasn’t even looked at me. He might be a little bit of a risk to keep around. Tiffany.Wasn’t she an athlete? I forget her story. But again, she worries me because she was on with Q. So that’s another trio: Charlie, Q and Tiffany.Right, though to be fair, they weren’t exactly that much of a group.That’s true too. But because they weren’t then doesn’t mean they won’t be now. Maybe they’ll think, “Oh, people aren’t gonna think we’re together.” Yeah. So anything can go.You mentioned Genevieve before as someone you want to get to know. Give me your thoughts on her. Genevieve, she seems to just be warm. She’s kind of giving me a warm smile. We were in the group walking in front of the airplane, and a couple of things happened. She laughed like one time at me when I did something stupid. I don’t know, she just seems kind of cool. Let’s get into this group we recently saw in Survivor 48. What are your thoughts on Joe?Love Joe. I loved him on the show. He reminds me of a Tom Westman. I feel like he would probably want to play with somebody like me who’s loyal and wants to play an honorable game too for my children. I can relate to Joe. His sister passed away. I had two brothers that passed away very unexpectedly. That’s big reason I’m out here. They were huge fans of mine. I grew up with four older brothers, only girl, youngest. And I lost them. One right after COVID, totally unexpected, heart attack. He was in his 50s. And then, almost a year later, another brother. Heart attack, same thing, awful. And my brothers, they were at all three live finales. Jeff knows them; people on the crew knew them. I mean, it’s why I am who I am. I’m toughest now because I was a tomboy growing up, and I had these brothers that loved me no matter what. But they just made me tough. They never fought my battles. They’re like, “You got a problem with him, her? Whatever, go [take care of it.] So I’m partly here for them. And then when Joe had the whole thing about his sister, I was like, “Oh my God, no way.” I would have said yes to 50 regardless; it’s 50. But I heard my brothers going, “Yeah, you’ve got to f—king do 50, Stephenie. Get the hell out there. Show them you still got it.” So I related to Joe on the show. So I hope he’ll want to get to know me.How about Kamilla?I loved her and Kyle. I can’t believe they’re both here, actually. I’m like, “Really, both of them are here?” I thought they would have done one or the other. And I loved the game they played. I almost feel like Cirie and I could play a little bit of a game like that. Even though people think we know each other, Cirie and I did that. In the castle, we didn’t even act like we knew each other. And it was just implied. We would have these quick talks when we could. You barely even saw us talking on camera. And because our camera crew is not as good as this camera crew, they never even caught us. And she’s like, “I’ll keep you safe if you keep me safe.” And you can never say you’re a Traitor. But basically, I knew it had to be one of us, and I knew it wasn’t me. Right, sort of the “Traitor Angel” strategy.Sandra coined that phrase; I just didn’t verbalize it. Already in my mind, I was like, “Cirie’s basically my Traitor Angel. She’s protecting me from the inside. Why would I f—king out her?” So I really respected Kamilla and Kyle’s game. She’s a huge threat. I mean, obviously, Kyle is because he won. But she’s almost like a Cirie. Keep her around long enough, she’ll win the whole thing. And she’s another one hasn’t really made eye contact with me. So I don’t know if she would even want to get to know me. I don’t know, she worries me. What are your opinions on the 49 players?There’s been rumors Savannah won, so we’ll see how true that is. I’ll see if I can get that out of Rizo. But it leads me to believe that if she won, he was probably runner-up or close behind. And either they’ve been working together, or they hate each other. So either way, I’d like to get to know both of them first before forming any opinions. But I do think an enemy that you know is easier to get rid of. At least you know what you got [versus] an enemy you don’t.Which previous player do you wish were out here on the island with you right now?[Pause.] Rafe. Honestly, he was such a great guy to bounce things off of. And I would say Tom, but we already played together in Heroes vs. Villains. We see how that played out. I thought maybe Rafe would maybe come back. He was only on one time. He was so brilliant. Truly, he knew the game inside. He’s a big reason I got to the end. And I just loved him, and I kept in touch with him for a really long time, and then I’ve kind of lost touch. But I follow him, and I see how successful he’s become. I hope he’s the next Mike White, or better. Finally, what celebrity or fictional character would you bring out for a Loved Ones visit? Boston Rob. Because I would just need some real, true advice. And he’d be the guy that would know it. About the authorMike Bloom has the great fortune of having parlayed decades of nerdom in movie and TV watching into almost a decade of writing and talking about it! Since joining Parade in 2017, Mike has largely covered reality television, becoming one of the go-to journalists for Survivor, Big Brother, The Amazing Race, Dancing with the Stars, Top Chef, The Challenge, and more.
